sheet-24-1.description: Lower half of sheet 24, a new sheet of April 1921 drawn at 60 feet to an inch, showing the beach blocks of Manasquan where East Main reaches the shore. North lies towards the right. East Main crosses the part diagonally from the upper left to 1st Avenue; 2nd Avenue (marked not graded) runs across the top and 1st Avenue across the lower half, parallel to the Atlantic Ocean shore along the bottom margin. Block 533 between the two avenues has a row of small frame dwellings facing 1st Avenue and, at East Main, a large pavilion and a group of dwellings set at an angle along East Main. Block 532 west of East Main has two automobile garages and a buried 550-gallon gasoline tank. South of 1st Avenue, block 536 holds a long row of beach cottages and The Seabird summer hotel near East Main, with automobile houses on the north side of 1st Avenue. A six-inch water pipe with hydrants is drawn in 1st Avenue. Blocks 526 and 531 north of 2nd Avenue are vacant, and the strip between the cottages and the water is open beach. The part continues on sheet 86 to the left and sheet 87 to the right; the compass rose and the scale bar are printed within it. The upper half of the sheet, with the key map of the town and the inset of the Biggets Park Hotel in Sea Girt, is not part of this annotation.
notes: East Main is Main Street today.
The upper half of the sheet holds the town key map (not georeferenced) and an inset of the Biggets Park Hotel by Wreck Pond in Sea Girt, left unplaced.

New sheet Apr 1921, 60 ft. Top left: location map and key map of the town (small scale, not georeferenced). Part 1 (bottom): beach blocks 531-536 on 1st and 2nd Avenues at East Main Street. Part 2 (inset, top right): Biggets Park Hotel lot by Wreck Pond, Sea Girt, at the Turnpike and Beacon Blvd; no printed scale.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Biggets Park Hotel by Wreck Pond, Sea Girt (Turnpike and Beacon Blvd) (one junction (Beacon Boulevard / 7th and 8th Avenue) at the inset's corner, no printed scale, no other feature that survives; needs hand-picked control from a modern feature of the hotel grounds or Wreck Pond shore, or an anchored fit on the Beacon Boulevard junction with an assumed 60 ft scale).

sheet-85.description: Additional sheet of April 1921, drawn at 120 feet to an inch, covering the newer residential tract on the east side of Manasquan between East Main and Stockton Lake. East Main runs down the left third of the sheet from Warren and Wyckoff Avenues at the top to below Potter Avenue at the bottom, with Euclid Avenue parallel to it on the west and Fletcher, Maclean and Lake Avenues parallel to it on the east. The cross streets, from the top, are Wyckoff, Minerva, Farragut, McClellan, Jackson and Potter Avenues. Stockton Lake Avenue curves along the east side above the shore of Stockton Lake, which fills the right margin. Below Potter Avenue, Rogers and Ocean Avenues begin and continue onto sheet 87. The blocks are laid out in narrow lots, most of them still vacant: the built lots carry frame dwellings with automobile houses behind, a few concrete-block outbuildings, and a poultry house. Named buildings are the Rosemary House on East Main at McClellan Avenue, the Jackson summer hotel on East Main between Jackson and Potter Avenues, and a cottage named Wayside on Potter Avenue. Four-inch and six-inch water pipes with hydrants are drawn in East Main, Fletcher, Lake, Potter and Ocean Avenues. Euclid Avenue south of Farragut is marked not graded, and the land west of it is open with only scattered buildings. Block numbers 501 to 525 are printed in the blocks; the adjoining sheets 31 and 87 are indicated at the top and bottom margins.
notes: East Main is Main Street today; the cross avenues are split into North and South Farragut, Mc Clellan, Jackson and Potter Avenues at Main Street in OpenStreetMap.
Maclean Avenue is Mc Lean Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Stockton Lake Avenue is Stockton Lake Boulevard.
Fletcher and Maclean Avenues begin at the lot line south of Minerva Avenue; the modern streets continue north to Minerva and Wyckoff.
Euclid Avenue junctions sit 3 to 4 m off the fit of the other streets and were left out of the control.
Minerva Avenue meets Stockton Lake Avenue about 11 m from the modern junction; that junction was rejected.

Add'l sheet Apr 1921, scale 120 ft to an inch. E. Main St from Warren/Wyckoff Av to below Potter Av, Euclid, Fletcher, Maclean, Lake, Stockton Lake, Rogers and Ocean Avs; Stockton Lake on the east. One part.

sheet-86-1.description: Left strip of sheet 86, an additional sheet of April 1921 drawn at 60 feet to an inch, showing the Manasquan beach front south of East Main, with north towards the top. 1st Avenue runs down the strip from East Main at the top margin, where the part continues from sheet 24, to the bottom margin, where it continues in the right strip of the same sheet. 2nd Avenue, marked not graded, runs parallel to it on the west as far as Park Avenue, the only cross street drawn. The west side of 1st Avenue (block 532 north of Park Avenue and block 529 south of it) is lined with small frame cottages numbered 224 to 264, and Park Avenue has a row of cottages on both sides, two of them named Freedom and Little Inn. On the ocean side of 1st Avenue (blocks 535 and 530) are cottages numbered 60 to 131 with automobile houses on the street front, a pavilion with outbuildings and a rifle range just south of East Main, and a row of houses set along a curving line south of Park Avenue. Six-inch and four-inch water pipes with hydrants are drawn in 1st Avenue. Deep Creek winds along the lower left, and the Atlantic Ocean shore runs down the right side of the strip next to the heavy line that divides the sheet. West of 2nd Avenue the land is vacant.
notes: Park Avenue is Brielle Road today.
East Main (Main Street) meets 1st Avenue just above the top margin; the junction was measured at the edge of the image.
Placed from two junctions on 1st Avenue, about 190 m apart; the fitted scale is 2.5 percent larger than the atlas scan constant.

Add'l sheet Apr 1921, 60 ft. Two strips divided by a heavy line: part 1 (left) 1st and 2nd Avs from E. Main to Park Av (now Brielle Road) and south along Deep Creek; part 2 (right) 1st Av continued south to the Manasquan River and breakwater, no cross street drawn.

sheet-86-2.description: Right strip of sheet 86, an additional sheet of April 1921 drawn at 60 feet to an inch, continuing the left strip of the same sheet: 1st Avenue on the Manasquan beach south from the foot of the left strip to the Manasquan River. North is towards the top. No cross street is drawn. The west side of 1st Avenue (block 529) has a thin row of frame cottages numbered 180 to 223, some with automobile houses or platforms behind; the east side (block 530) has automobile houses on the street front numbered with the suffix A and a denser row of beach cottages numbered 132 to 178 facing the ocean, several of them named, among them the Savoy, The Ruth, Speed Inn, Poughkeepsie, Rosita, The Pekin and Ruff Wood. A four-inch water pipe with hydrants runs in 1st Avenue. The Atlantic Ocean shore runs down the right margin. At the bottom the Manasquan River crosses the strip diagonally, with a break water along its north bank, and 1st Avenue ends at the river. The left part of the strip, beyond the lots on the west side of 1st Avenue, is empty.
notes: No street junction is drawn; the part is placed from a building drawn at the foot of the left strip and again at the head of this strip, at the scan scale and the rotation of the left strip. Low confidence along 1st Avenue.
The break water and river bank predate the present Manasquan Inlet jetties.

Add'l sheet Apr 1921, 60 ft. Two strips divided by a heavy line: part 1 (left) 1st and 2nd Avs from E. Main to Park Av (now Brielle Road) and south along Deep Creek; part 2 (right) 1st Av continued south to the Manasquan River and breakwater, no cross street drawn.

sheet-87-1.description: Upper part of sheet 87, an additional sheet of April 1921 drawn at 60 feet to an inch, south of sheet 85 on the east side of Manasquan, with north towards the upper right. Rogers Avenue and Ocean Avenue run diagonally down from the top margin, where they continue from sheet 85. Rogers Avenue ends at a lot line north of Watsons Creek; Ocean Avenue crosses the creek on a short bridge and continues to 2nd Avenue at the bottom of the part. Between and beside the two avenues are the long, narrow lots of blocks 523, 524 and 527, with frame dwellings and automobile houses lining both sides of Ocean Avenue, a small pink-coloured brick building at the top, and a boat house and a concrete-block building on the creek. A four-inch water pipe with a hydrant is drawn in Ocean Avenue. Block 526 west of Ocean Avenue and south of the creek, and the land east of the creek, are vacant and carry only a zero for no buildings. Watsons Creek crosses the part from the left margin to the lower right, where it turns north. A compass rose and the sheet title are printed in the vacant lower left.
notes: Sheet 87 is drawn as one map but georeferenced as two parts: the upper half fits Rogers Avenue only at a rotation about 5 degrees from the one that fits 1st Avenue in the lower half.
Placed from the 2nd Avenue / Ocean Avenue junction of part 2 and two points on the modern line of Rogers Avenue, which fits sheet 85 to 4 m; low confidence along Rogers Avenue.
East Main is only named in the top left margin.

Add'l sheet Apr 1921, 60 ft. Ocean and Rogers Avs south of sheet 85, Watsons Creek, 2nd and 1st Avs at Ocean Av with U.S. Coast Guard Station 105. Drawn as one map, configured as two parts divided along 2nd Av: part 1 (Rogers/Ocean across the creek) fits modern Rogers Av only about 5 degrees from the rotation that fits 1st Av in part 2 (beach blocks).

sheet-87-2.description: Lower part of sheet 87, an additional sheet of April 1921 drawn at 60 feet to an inch, covering the beach front of Manasquan at the foot of Ocean Avenue, east of sheet 24. North lies towards the right. 2nd Avenue runs across the top of the part and 1st Avenue across the middle, parallel to the Atlantic Ocean shore along the bottom margin; Ocean Avenue comes down from 2nd Avenue as a narrow way to 1st Avenue. Blocks 533 and 536 west of Ocean Avenue hold rows of small frame cottages facing 1st Avenue, with automobile houses on the north side of the street, and the Pine-Maple Cottage stands at the corner of 2nd and Ocean Avenues. East of Ocean Avenue, between 2nd Avenue and the beach, is the U.S. Coast Guards Station 105, drawn with its station house and tower, cistern, storage and ice house, a second storage building, fishermans quarters, a mess house, a fish market, a buried 550-gallon gasoline tank, an oil house and a lookout tower on the dune. Block 534 north of the station is vacant, and block 537 by the beach has a few scattered cottages, one named Our Own. Six-inch and four-inch water pipes are drawn in 1st Avenue and Ocean Avenue. East of the Coast Guard lot, 1st Avenue is drawn south of its line west of Ocean Avenue. The scale bar is printed at the lower right.
notes: 1st Avenue east of the Coast Guard station lot is drawn south of its line west of Ocean Avenue.

Placed from the 2nd Avenue / Ocean Avenue and 1st Avenue / Ocean Avenue junctions at the scan scale, with rotation from the lines measured at 1st Avenue; agrees with the modern line of 1st Avenue to 3 m.

Add'l sheet Apr 1921, 60 ft. Ocean and Rogers Avs south of sheet 85, Watsons Creek, 2nd and 1st Avs at Ocean Av with U.S. Coast Guard Station 105. Drawn as one map, configured as two parts divided along 2nd Av: part 1 (Rogers/Ocean across the creek) fits modern Rogers Av only about 5 degrees from the rotation that fits 1st Av in part 2 (beach blocks).
